title: Ophir Co Limited - Monthly Exploration Report May 2026
content: Monthly Exploration Report For Ophir Co Limited. Geologist: Sampson Nsiah. Date: 30th May 2026. Confidential information, no disclosure.

title: May 2026 Project Details
content: Licence Number: SSML04-2024/06/20-09. Project Name: CAMP15 PROJECT. Type of Report: MONTHLY REPORT. Reporting Period: (01/05/2026) to (31/05/2026). Author: SAMPSON NSIAH. License Name: ML. CEO: OPHIR COMPANY LIMITED. Primary Mineral: GOLD.

title: May 2026 Regional Geology - Eastern Equatoria
content: Eastern Equatoria sits on Precambrian Basement of East African Orogen (Mozambique Belt). Reworked in Pan-African Orogeny ~550-900 Ma. Main units: A. Precambrian Basement Complex - Gneisses, migmatites, schists, high-grade metamorphics - granitic gneiss, biotite-hornblende gneiss, amphibolite. Meta-volcanics and meta-sediments: Quartz-mica schist, quartzite ridges. Granitoids: Late Pan-African granites (pink, coarse, phaneritic). Mafic rocks: Pyroxene-rich gabbro/dolerite dykes, amphibolite. B. Cenozoic Volcanics: Tertiary basalts and trachytes (near Ethiopia border, Didinga Hills). C. Quaternary Cover: Alluvium, laterite (2-10m thick), black cotton soil.

title: May 2026 2016 Geological Study - Nimule
content: 2016 geological study (Nimule): Station 15a: Granitic rock (quartz, K-feldspar, biotite, <5% plagioclase). Station 15b and 16: Mafic igneous (quartz + plagioclase, pyroxene-dominated, <10% biotite). Fine-medium grained, greenish, ophitic texture with pyroxene + opaque magnetite/ilmenite.

title: May 2026 Kapoeta Area Geology
content: Kapoeta area: Precambrian gneiss and schist basement. Didinga Hills: Hydrothermally altered basement with potential for gold. Satellite gravity + remote sensing used to map alteration zones. Economic Geology: Gold confirmed; NW-SE and NNE trending faults/dykes.

title: May 2026 Local Geological Setting - Camp 15
content: Camp 15 within Precambrian basement of East African Orogen. Host rocks: Quartz-biotite gneiss, locally sheared. Structure: NW-SE trending fault/shear zone, striking 267 degrees to 319 degrees, dipping ~65 degrees SW. Mineralization style: 2m wide quartz-carbonate breccia with gossan at surface. Alteration: Strong Fe-oxide after sulphides, silica-chlorite, mica, feldspar. Geo-chem signature from rock chips: boxwork after pyrite/arsenopyrite.

title: May 2026 Work Completed
content: Work Completed: Desk Study, Geological Mapping (Ongoing), Rock Chip Sampling Ongoing. Samples: C15R031 to C15R098. Total Samples Collected: 67. 3 QA/QC Samples, total Samples = 70.

title: May 2026 Mapping Features
content: Mapping Features: Brecciated quartz vein: ~2m width, ~150m strike length. Shear zone. Strongly foliated gneiss. Artisanal mining stream. Smoky to milky brecciated quartz vein. Fe-oxide stains, feldspar. ~7m width. Brecciated peg with qtz and feldspar dominant. E-W Structure: Brecciated, jointed, shear. Quartz vein, possible mesh zone.

title: May 2026 Gold Samples
content: Gold from stream few meters from camp. Gold speck from crushed sample (seen under lens). Brecciated quartz vein from stream.

title: May 2026 Geological Observations
content: Rock: Medium-coarse grained quartz-biotite gneiss with strong NW-SE foliation. Mineralized Zone: 2m wide quartz-carbonate-Fe-oxide breccia traced 150m along 319 degree trend. Complete oxidation of massive to semi-massive sulphides. Abundant boxwork after pyrite +/- arsenopyrite. Alteration Halo: Bleaching and silica-sericite alteration extends 1-3m into gneissic wallrock. Structure: Breccia along steep SW-dipping fault, pre-existing structure reactivated. Structural control: Regional NW-SE fault. Width: 2m+ true width indicates significant fluid flow.

title: May 2026 Recommendations
content: Recommendations: 1. Remote sensing mapping. 2. Extend mapping 200m NW and SE along structure. 3. Trenching at 50m spacing across breccia for channel samples/true width. 4. Drilling: If trench results >1 g/t Au, plan 4 x 60m DD holes to test 50m below surface.
